claims.head: The Penguins should drive the play
claims.body: The Penguins have been near the top of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Sharks one of the worst. Expect the Penguins to spend more of the night in the Sharks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

claims.head: Crash the net vs. Bombs away
claims.body: On shots from in close, Pittsburgh is the league’s best, but San Jose is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Penguins to do more of their damage around the net.

notes.text: Trevor van Riemsdyk is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 13 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Declan Carlile has taken his spot beside Kris Letang. That pair has had 55% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 77:55 together, up from 39% with van Riemsdyk.

Elmer Söderblom is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 6 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Nick Robertson has taken his spot beside Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte. That line has had 49% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 50:06 together.
Ville Koivunen is day to day (lower-body injury) and missed their last game.

Bryan Rust is on injured reserve and has missed the last 8 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. That line has had 58% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 66:42 together, up from 43% with Rust.
Ilya Solovyov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.
Nick Robertson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 28% of the team’s shorthanded time in 18 games, up from 2% with his old team last season.
Spencer Stastney is no longer killing penalties: 5% of the team’s shorthanded time in 13 games, down from 31% with his old team last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 22% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the lowest share in the league (a typical team: 40%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Igor Chernyshov is on injured reserve and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Michael Misa has taken his spot beside Will Smith and Macklin Celebrini. That line has had 48% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 30:38 together, down from 60% with Chernyshov.
Alexander Wennberg has not dressed for the last 10 games. He is a top-six forward.
Alexander Wennberg is expected back after missing 10 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Filip Bystedt was added to the roster on Oct 29 and has played beside Tyler Toffoli and Ivar Stenberg.
Eric Pohlkamp was added to the roster on Nov 4 and has played beside Dmitry Orlov.

SJS.head: Not an easy night for the Sharks
SJS.body: Even though San Jose has home-ice advantage and Pittsburgh may be without Koivunen, the Penguins have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Sharks can pull it off if they get good looks.

PIT.head: The Penguins should have the upper hand
PIT.body: Even though San Jose has home-ice advantage and Pittsburgh may be without Koivunen, the Penguins have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Sharks’ way back in is getting good looks.

story.head: Somebody has to win
paras: The Sharks are on a five-game losing streak, and the Penguins (6-10-2) lost 5-2 to Anaheim on Sunday. Both teams are near the bottom of the standings. Going in, the Pens are seventh in the Metropolitan (tied for 27th in the NHL) and the Sharks sixth in the Pacific (26th).

The Penguins have played better than their record (.389) says: their chances are worth about .549, mostly because they’re 3-6 in one-goal games. The Sharks’ record (.395) is about what their chances are worth.

The Penguins sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest), get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and rarely throw hits (lowest). As for the Sharks, they ice the puck a lot (32nd) and have a leaky penalty kill (30th). They also do a lot of their shooting from distance (4th lowest), so the Penguins get in close, but them mostly shoot from distance. San Jose has scored 2.47 goals a game, the third fewest in the league, and allowed 3.58, the fourth most. The Penguins are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Sharks.

Erik Karlsson (3 G / 15 A / 18 P in 18 GP) leads the Penguins in scoring. Tommy Novak (7 G / 7 A / 14 P in 18 GP) has a team-high seven goals, with five goals in seven games against San Jose since 2023-24. For the Sharks, Macklin Celebrini (7 G / 14 A / 21 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring.
Artūrs Šilovs (5-6-1 / .873 SV% in 12 GS) will likely start for Pittsburgh, and Yaroslav Askarov (4-8-0 / .885 SV% in 12 GS) for San Jose.
The Penguins usually control more of the chances than the Sharks do.

items.text: Sidney Crosby has a point in six straight games against San Jose, with a goal in each of the last four.

The Penguins are newly without Ville Koivunen, and have been without Trevor van Riemsdyk, Elmer Söderblom and Bryan Rust for several games. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Mammoth are missing more right now.
The Sharks have been without Igor Chernyshov and Alexander Wennberg for several games.
With Alexander Wennberg out, Collin Graf took 13 faceoffs in the Sharks’ last game. He had been taking fewer than one a game.
